items.t: I am broadly neutral on the trans-girls-in-sports question and think it’s emblematic of culture-war wedge issues that won’t affect many people being turned into political weapons. That said. When the USWNT, best in the world, scrimmages with teams of 14-15-year-old boys, they often lose. The Williams sisters, at the peak of their powers in the late 90s, played the something-like-200th-ranked man in the world and lost. And the people who say things like “there’s no physical difference between men and women in athletics, it’s all conservative propaganda” get furious if you point that out and come up with all kinds of ways it doesn’t count. Do conservatives make too much hay out of it, because they’re bigots in general, yes, absolutely, no disagreement here. But trans-girls-should-play-boys-sports was like, the only left-wing thing that got roundly rejected at the polls last week in the middle of an otherwise-humiliating showing for conservatives. “It’s just conservative propaganda” does not seem to cut it as an answer. You can argue a position you find morally correct without pretending everyone already agrees with you. “Every decent, serious person agrees with my obviously true position, it’s insulting that I’m even being asked to defend it” does not have a great track record recently.
